items.title: WE TESTED FOUR FRONTIER AI MODELS ON REAL PATIENT PRESCRIPTIONS. NONE ACHIEVED 100% ACCURACY.
items.summary:
WE TESTED FOUR FRONTIER AI MODELS ON REAL PATIENT PRESCRIPTIONS. NONE ACHIEVED 100% ACCURACY.

At Xpert Systems Inc., we have completed Frontier Model Breaker Test 19 — Prescription Safety Review, a clinical reasoning benchmark built using real, de-identified outpatient records.

THE DATASET:

26 real patient records
421 longitudinal outpatient visits
72 real prescriptions selected for evaluation
4 frontier AI models tested
5 required answers per prescription

Unlike benchmarks built around invented patients and simplified medical histories, our evaluation uses actual de-identified patient records containing medication histories, allergies, diagnoses, adverse reactions, and clinical notes.

Each AI model must determine:

Should the prescription be REJECTED, HELD, PENDED, or APPROVED?
Which safety rule determines the decision?
Which additional safety rules apply?
What evidence supports the decision?
What single change would alter the decision?

THE RESULTS — STRICT ACCURACY:

GPT-5.6 Terra: 95.8%

GPT-5.6 Luna: 94.4%

Claude Haiku 4.5: 86.1%

Claude Sonnet 5: 84.7%

Strict accuracy requires all five answers to be correct.

NONE OF THE FOUR MODELS ACHIEVED A PERFECT OVERALL SCORE.

More importantly, two models incorrectly approved one prescription each that should have been held, pended, or rejected under the benchmark policy.

The evaluation exposed failures involving duplicate medications, older-adult safety checks, allergy interpretation, incomplete evidence, and incorrect rule application.

WHY DOES THIS MATTER?

Healthcare AI needs more than medical knowledge. It must reliably interpret longitudinal patient histories and apply safety policies without overlooking critical details.

WE ARE OFFERING THIS BENCHMARK FOR COMMERCIAL LICENSING.

Our evaluation package includes de-identified records, ground-truth answers, an independent checker, automated scoring, and model evaluation tools.

CALLING FRONTIER AI LABS, HEALTHCARE AI COMPANIES, PHARMACY SOFTWARE VENDORS, AND FOUNDATION MODEL DEVELOPERS!

DM me or write to pradeep@xpertsystems.ai to request the evaluation kit and discuss licensing.

https://t.co/m25kbCPtn9

This is a research benchmark using simplified safety policies, not a clinically validated prescribing system. Human clinical oversight remains essential.

items.title: State Superintendent Tony Thurmond Convenes Summit on AI in Education, Emphasizes Innovation, Student Safety, and Educator Leadership - The Santa Barbara Independent
items.summary: California is also advancing statewide efforts to establish a responsible framework for AI use in K–12 education. Senate Bill 1288, sponsored by Superintendent Thurmond, established a statewide AI working group charged with developing guidance and a model policy for local educational agencies. This work will help schools navigate emerging technologies while addressing student privacy, data security, academic integrity, and the appropriate role of AI in teaching and learning. [...] “California has an opportunity to lead the nation in demonstrating how AI can be used responsibly to strengthen teaching and learning,” said Superintendent Thurmond. “But innovation cannot come at the expense of student safety, privacy, or the human connections that are essential to education. We must be thoughtful about when and how these tools are used, ensure educators remain at the center of instructional decisions, and demand evidence that technology is actually improving student outcomes. [...] The summit reflected California’s balanced approach to AI in education: exploring the potential of emerging technologies to support student achievement while recognizing the need for clear safeguards, equitable access, educator involvement, and accountability for results.

items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] With this recent update to extensive, existing policy on AI, the AMA House of Delegates calls for AI-enabled technologies to be integrated into physician-led teams and used at the direction of the treating physician. AI tools used for clinical functions such as diagnosis, prescribing and care management should have transparent, auditable evidence demonstrating their safety and efficacy and be subject to appropriate regulation, documentation and liability requirements. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.”

items.title: Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing
items.summary:
This would value Anthropic at between $1.1 trillion and $1.3 trillion which, although large, is below the $2 trillion some analysts had predicted weeks ago.

It is floating at a volatile time for AI firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres.

There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off. [...] Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the amount Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week".

She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there."

## Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe [...] # Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing

Getty Images Claude by Anthropic logo on a smartphone 

Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, is planning to raise up to $64bn (£48bn) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.

The loss-making company said it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each in its initial public offering (IPO), which is expected to go ahead this month.

items.title: Việt Nam - Nhật Bản hoàn tất chuyển giao công nghệ tế bào trị ung thư
items.summary:
Công nghệ tế bào gốc trung mô (MSC) hiện được nghiên cứu, phát triển trong nhiều hướng ứng dụng liên quan đến bệnh lý tim mạch, thần kinh (đột quỵ, sa sút trí tuệ), tiểu đường, bệnh phổi tắc nghẽn mạn tính (COPD), trẻ hóa da… Giải pháp tế bào miễn dịch tự nhiên (NK) mở ra cơ hội ứng dụng mới trong miễn dịch trị liệu, có thể được phối hợp với các phương pháp điều trị ung thư đa mô thức khác, như phẫu thuật, hóa trị, xạ trị và điều trị đích. [...] Hai bên lựa chọn chuyển giao các công nghệ tế bào thế hệ mới, được Tập đoàn Y tế Grandsoul, Nhật Bản nghiên cứu, phát triển và ứng dụng. Bộ Y tế, Lao động và Phúc lợi Nhật Bản (MHLW) đã phê duyệt, cấp phép ứng dụng chính thức nhiều năm tại nước này. Trọng tm gồm hai nhóm: công nghệ phn lập, nuôi cấy, biệt hóa chọn lọc tế bào gốc trung mô có nguồn gốc từ mô mỡ (Mesenchymal Stem Cells - MSC) và công nghệ phn lập nuôi cấy, biệt hóa chọn lọc tế bào miễn dịch tự nhiên NK (Natural Killer cells) điều [...] ### Từ tiếp nhận công nghệ đến năng lực tự chủ tại Việt Nam

Ông Ngô Chí Dũng, Chủ tịch HĐQT Hệ thống Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tm Anh, cho biết việc hoàn tất chuyển giao công nghệ tế bào gốc và tế bào miễn dịch từ Nhật Bản là dấu mốc quan trọng không chỉ trong hợp tác y tế hai nước, mà còn là kết nối công nghệ, thiết lập mạng lưới chuyên gia vì mục tiêu chung là chăm sóc sức khỏe cho người dn.

items.title: Thúc đẩy ứng dụng công nghệ sinh học, tạo đột phá cho nông nghiệp Việt Nam

Theo Tiến sĩ Nguyễn Văn Long, định hướng phát triển và ứng dụng công nghệ sinh học tại Việt Nam đã được cụ thể hóa thông qua nhiều chủ trương, chính sách quan trọng, nổi bật là Nghị quyết số 36-NQ/TW năm 2023 về phát triển và ứng dụng công nghệ sinh học và Nghị quyết số 57-NQ/TW năm 2024 về đột phá phát triển khoa học, công nghệ, đổi mới sáng tạo và chuyển đổi số quốc gia. [...] Năm 2024, diện tích canh tác cy trồng ứng dụng công nghệ sinh học toàn cầu đạt khoảng 287 triệu ha, cho thấy xu hướng ứng dụng ngày càng rộng rãi của công nghệ này. items.title: Experts Explore How AI Could Affect Vulnerable Communities, Social Service Providers - UConn Today
items.summary:
“Sometimes, the right tool for the task is something simple, like a book in the hands of a child, sitting on his parent’s lap,” she said.

Broussard also cautioned against assuming that AI can replace professional expertise or operate indefinitely without human attention. She discussed model drift—the potential for a model’s performance to deteriorate as circumstances change—and the ongoing work required to maintain reliable systems. [...] In health care, she pointed to AI assisting radiologists as a promising application, emphasizing the importance of keeping clinicians involved in interpreting results. She encouraged social work researchers to consider how the technology could support their own expertise.

“Don’t expect it to replace humans, but do think about the ways that AI can augment your analysis,” she said.

Her closing message emphasized that people have choices about whether, where, and how to adopt the technology. [...] “Technochauvinists say AI is keeps getting better. It is getting better, actually and I say, yes they are right. It does keep getting better, but it’s never going to become good. It’s not going to achieve human level. It’s not. Because it’s a computer. It’s a machine,” she said. “We need to have a more nuanced view.”

items.title: State Superintendent Tony Thurmond Convenes Summit on AI in Education, Emphasizes Innovation, Student Safety, and Educator Leadership - The Santa Barbara Independent
items.summary: California is also advancing statewide efforts to establish a responsible framework for AI use in K–12 education. Senate Bill 1288, sponsored by Superintendent Thurmond, established a statewide AI working group charged with developing guidance and a model policy for local educational agencies. This work will help schools navigate emerging technologies while addressing student privacy, data security, academic integrity, and the appropriate role of AI in teaching and learning. [...] “California has an opportunity to lead the nation in demonstrating how AI can be used responsibly to strengthen teaching and learning,” said Superintendent Thurmond. “But innovation cannot come at the expense of student safety, privacy, or the human connections that are essential to education. We must be thoughtful about when and how these tools are used, ensure educators remain at the center of instructional decisions, and demand evidence that technology is actually improving student outcomes. [...] The summit reflected California’s balanced approach to AI in education: exploring the potential of emerging technologies to support student achievement while recognizing the need for clear safeguards, equitable access, educator involvement, and accountability for results.

items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] With this recent update to extensive, existing policy on AI, the AMA House of Delegates calls for AI-enabled technologies to be integrated into physician-led teams and used at the direction of the treating physician. AI tools used for clinical functions such as diagnosis, prescribing and care management should have transparent, auditable evidence demonstrating their safety and efficacy and be subject to appropriate regulation, documentation and liability requirements. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.”

items.title: Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing
items.summary:
This would value Anthropic at between $1.1 trillion and $1.3 trillion which, although large, is below the $2 trillion some analysts had predicted weeks ago.

It is floating at a volatile time for AI firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres.

There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off. [...] Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the amount Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week".

She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there."

## Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe [...] # Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing

Getty Images Claude by Anthropic logo on a smartphone 

Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, is planning to raise up to $64bn (£48bn) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.

The loss-making company said it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each in its initial public offering (IPO), which is expected to go ahead this month.

[...] Robots struggle to adapt to new unpredictable environments, our Gemini Robotics models give Apollo the ability to think, reason over multiple steps, and take action adapting to changes. In this proof-of-concept, Apollo 2 autonomously performs automotive kitting: the repetitive, physically taxing task of sorting individual parts from bulk bins into organized trays in the exact order needed for each vehicle on the line. Offloading this monotonous prep work helps keep the assembly line moving, [...] With Gemini Robotics 2.5, we expanded the model capabilities in task breadth, performance, and complexity. We evaluated the model across 200 distinct tasks — such as serving food with tongs, tying a bow on a gift box, and pipetting a liquid. These tasks represent a step toward human-level dexterity by combining a number of skills, including advanced tool use, complex manipulation of deformables, and handling delicate objects with finesse.

items.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak" - Ars Technica
items.summary: DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate. [...] Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. [...] Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version. It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.

Stork Labs Medical, based in Sacramento and Santa Cruz, is an emerging biomedical startup developing the Pelican device: a flexible, sensor-guided soft robotics tool created to make assisted vaginal deliveries safer and reduce emergency C-sections. The device is designed to spread force more evenly across the baby’s head to help prevent injury and give doctors real-time guidance with integrated sensors, says Maryam Tebyani, the company’s co-founder and CEO. items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.
